Source & image record ↗ · CC BY 2.0

Exact item identifies Kettle Point in Ontario projecting into Lake Huron. The Nation’s History & Culture page places Kettle Point on the lake’s south shore and links the place name to shoreline rocks. The full photo also includes surrounding agricultural land; no reserve boundary or Stony Point view is inferred. These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Reading day-school history with community participation

Jordan George, Jackson Pind and Benjamin Farmer Lacombe link the 1942 displacement at Stony Point to the day school’s closure and pupils’ relocation to Kettle Point. Their community-coauthored article also describes petitions and withheld attendance over teacher misconduct, bringing community responses into an archive largely produced by colonial officials.

Read the sources [2] Cultural and Pedagogical Inquiry, University of Alberta, 15(2), 68–81

02

Language in radio and digital learning

The Eagle’s community-hosted description links radio with language, stories, local news and musicians; its anniversary statement refers to 2013. George and his collaborators separately describe translating a day-school website interface into Anishinaabemowin. They note that English-only records and uneven handwriting recognition continued to limit archival access.

Read the sources [1] Chippewas of Kettle & Stony Point First Nation [2] Cultural and Pedagogical Inquiry, University of Alberta, 15(2), 68–81

The Eagle 107.7 FM — Radio Station ↗

The station’s mission and service account connects local news, language, stories and musicians. Its anniversary statement explicitly refers to 2013, so operating details are not treated as a current schedule.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual Mission Statement, Services and About the Eagle text, web lines 11–22. Contact hours and linked station content excluded from substantive use.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

Kettle and Stony Point First Nation: A Narrative of Indigenous Language Revitalization and Digital Indian Day School Histories ↗

Publication: 2024-11-13

Jordan George, Jackson Pind and Benjamin Farmer Lacombe link community school history with an Anishinaabemowin digital interface. Their account also exposes language and handwriting biases in colonial archives.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual PDF printed 69–79: author positionalities, school history, translation process and technical biases; title/abstract and bibliography inspected. Publisher landing page read for author and release metadata.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
